2050.unvetted: Scan needs a Gilder Lehrman subscriber login or a PDF order (Chrome opened glc00537; not signed in). Record: 'Union cipher letter written on stationery of the Head Quarters of Army of the Potomac, office of the Chief Quarter Master', 1 p. + docket, 12 Dec 1862, English. The small dimmed public preview shows letterhead, an address to J. W. Nesmith at Washington, about seven lines of running words and a signature, no numerals: too dim to read, and not enough to judge. Check when the page is open: this may be Chinook Jargon, not a cipher. chinookjargon.com prints retellings (e.g. Harrisburg Patriot, 13 Mar 1882) of Ingalls wiring Nesmith in Chinook just before Fredericksburg, with an English translation but no original wording. Those retellings describe a telegram and do not cite this letter, so no not_cipher yet. known.py: only this lead.
